final.memo:
Our original thesis—that Yahoo suffered from a massive valuation gap between its core internet business and its Asian assets, compounded by stagnant leadership—has evolved significantly. Through our governance campaign, we successfully secured board access and a new CEO [D03], [D07]. With the primary governance catalyst now realized, our involvement is naturally transitioning to a close [D07]. 

While Asian assets continue to provide distinct upside, the core advertising business remains in a difficult spot, with revenue and adjusted EBITDA declining [D01], [D03]. The company’s focus has shifted to product development and mobile engagement, but these efforts have yet to translate into a proven turnaround in margins or core growth [D03], [D05]. We are not prepared to credit the rising share price solely to these nascent operational improvements [D03]. 

We have been presented with liquidity terms for a block of shares at $29.11, offering a premium to current market levels [D02], [D04]. Given that our board-service role is concluding and the easy governance wins are behind us, it is prudent to trim our position [D07]. This allows us to lock in gains and redeploy capital toward higher-skew events, rather than waiting for an unproven product turnaround to manifest [D04], [D05].
